root_causes.evidence: Primary screening p95 was about 1800 ms against a 15 ms baseline. Payments calls to it errored at 53-96% while payments itself was unchanged. After failover the standby answers in about 15 ms with 0 errors.
Clearing was down after exit code 15 (SIGTERM) and logged no errors. Its head item had 0 attempts, so it is not poison. After a restart it processed 2.37/s and the queue drained from 16 to 1.

sbar.situation: The bank payment system has recovered. Screening is now served by its standby, clearing is running again, and two recovery checks in a row came back clean, the last at 39 s.
sbar.background: Primary screening slowed to a p95 of about 1800 ms against a 15 ms baseline, so payments calls to it errored at 53-96%. Separately, clearing stopped after exit code 15 (SIGTERM), with no errors logged.
sbar.assessment: The incident commander took both actions itself. It failed screening over to the standby, which now answers in about 15 ms with 0 errors. It also restarted clearing, which now processes 2.37/s and has drained its queue from 16 to 1; the head item had 0 attempts, so it was not a poison message.
sbar.recommendation: Investigate why primary screening is slow, likely its network link, before failing back to it. Also find out what sent SIGTERM to clearing. Operations should review the payments that errored during the screening slowdown and confirm the items that were queued in clearing completed correctly.
